page.layout: Running head at top with page number at left. Below it, two engraved coin medallions side by side, with their legends printed around the rims. Then one column of text with two paragraphs, full width, no margin notes.

main_text.p: IO ANNES, Manuelis Palæologi filij, filius natu maior, post mortem patris in imperio succedit Constantinopolitano, circiter annum mundi 5395. à Christo nato 1433. Paci hic ac concordiæ magis quàm bello studens,comitatus totius Græcię comitibus, cùm sacris, tum profanis , atque Eugenij huius nominis quarti Pontificis autoritatem sccutus[?], Ferrariensi, quod deinde Florentiam translatum est, concilio interfuit : suscep-túsque est ab Eugenio Imperatorum more: atque ex duabus, nempe Græcorum ac Latinorum Ecclesiis, una facta est. Tunc à Græcis ac Latinis de processione Spiritus sancti damnatus est error.Reversus Imperator,haud ita diu supervixit. Vide Egna. lib.2.& Cosmog.Munst.lib.4.Plati.& Volater.

CONSTANTINVS, septimus Manuelis filius, mortuo sine liberis fratre Ioanne supradicto, Constantinopoli imperat, circiter annum mundi 5406. à Christo nato 1447. hic ab initio Peloponnesi Rex,Draconis cognomen inditum accepit, ob eam quam in Turcas exercebat ferocitatem. At verò à Mahomete Amurathis secundi filio capta Constantinopoli, ipse Constantinus ad portam trepidus se recipiens,fugientium trepidatione oppressus obiit:cuius caput pilo affixum,totis castris ad ludibrium hostis gestauit: anno mundi 5414. à Christo nato 1452. Id mirum , atque in fatis quasi habendum , nempe quòd à Constantino Magno Helenæ filio Constantinopolis, urbs Romæ semper æmula, condita aut instaurata sit, ac sub Constantino, qui eiusdem nominis matrem haberet, capta, Turcarúmque iugo ad hanc diem sit subdita. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions above the text, showing profile portraits of Ioannes (left) and Constantinus (right, with a double-faced or two-headed portrait). The legends around the medallion rims are part of the engravings and are given as the first two lines. Doubtful readings: "sccutus" (the word is possibly "fccutus"; long s is written as s). Printed spelling and printing errors are kept as they stand, such as "Ferrarien-" and "Reuersus" corrected to "Reversus" per the u/v rule, and "superuixit" corrected to "supervixit".
